Liga (Slovakia)|2025–26]] | position = 4th of 16 | website = {{URL|https://www.fcpetrzalka.sk/}}| | pattern_la1 = _black_stripes | pattern_b1 = _blackstripes | pattern_ra1 = _black_stripes | pattern_so1 = | leftarm1 = FFFFFF | body1 = FFFFFF | rightarm1 = FFFFFF | shorts1 = 000000 | socks1 = FFFFFF | pattern_la2 = _shoulder_stripes_black_stripes_half | pattern_b2 = _shoulder_stripes_black_stripes | pattern_ra2 = _shoulder_stripes_black_stripes_half | pattern_so2 = _3_stripes_black | leftarm2 = FFFFFF | body2 = FFFFFF | rightarm2 = FFFFFF | shorts2 = 000000 | socks2 = FFFFFF| }} '''FC Petržalka''' is a [[Slovakia|Slovak]] [[association football|football]] club based in [[Bratislava]]. The club was founded in 1898 and it was promoted twice to the top flight [[Czechoslovak First League|1. liga]] in the [[Czechoslovakia]] during the 1980s (for the [[1981–82 Czechoslovak First League|1981–82]] season and [[1984–85 Czechoslovak First League|1984–85]] season) and spent another 14 consecutive seasons in the [[Slovak First Football League|Slovak first league]] from 1996–97 to 2009–10. The biggest international success of Petržalka was participation in the group stage of the [[2005–06 UEFA Champions League]] and Round of 32 of the [[2005–06 UEFA Cup#Round of 32|2005–06 UEFA Cup]]. Several years later, after losing its owner, a different company took over the piece of land under the club's old home ground [[Štadión Petržalka]] for commercial building and the stadium was demolished.{{Cite web|url=http://www.4thegame.com/features/feature/226295/.html |title=On The Continent: The Fall of Artmedia |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090707025340/http://www.4thegame.com/features/feature/226295/.html |archive-date=7 July 2009}} The football club founded in 1898, from the previous sport club Pozsonyi Torna Egyesület which was grounded in 1880, initially played in the regional [[Kingdom of Hungary|Hungarian]] league.{{Cite news|title=Art Attack Artmedia Bratislava:A colourful past|work=[[Sunday Herald]]|date=16 October 2005|author=Stewart Fisher}} The club has been known by 17 names in its history, including Artmedia Bratislava (after their advertising agency sponsors).{{Cite web |url=http://www.fifa.com/tournaments/archive/tournament=107/edition=4735/news/newsid=100563.html |title=Artmedia, more than a name |access-date=21 April 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121110060221/http://www.fifa.com/tournaments/archive/tournament=107/edition=4735/news/newsid=100563.html |archive-date=10 November 2012 |url-status=dead }} Artmedia played in the top flight [[Slovak First Football League|Slovak league]] from its inception in 1993 until 2010. The club achieved its biggest success in the mid-2000s (decade), while playing under the coach [[Vladimír Weiss (footballer, born 1964)|Vladimír Weiss]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/tournaments/archive/tournament=107/edition=4735/news/newsid=100563.html |title=Artmedia, more than a name |publisher=FIFA.com |date=27 September 2005 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121110060221/http://www.fifa.com/tournaments/archive/tournament%3D107/edition%3D4735/news/newsid%3D100563.html |archive-date=10 November 2012 |url-status=dead }} The club won the Corgoň Liga title in 2005 and later qualified for the group stage of the Champions League, where it achieved the biggest success of all the Slovak clubs. Later, in 2008 the club won the [[Double (association football)|double]], but during the next season most of the squad left the club.{{Cite web|url=http://www.uefa.com/competitions/uefacup/news/kind=1/newsid=753322.html |title=Ravens gathering around stricken Artmedia |publisher=UEFA |date=23 September 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100126111805/http://www.uefa.com/competitions/uefacup/news/kind%3D1/newsid%3D753322.html |archive-date=26 January 2010 |url-status=dead }} The club plays its home matches at its own new [[Stadium FC Petržalka 1898|stadium]] with a capacity of 1600. The team wears white and black striped shirts. In 2025, the club expressed interest in building a new stadium.{{Cite web |title=Magistrát ponúkol FC Petržalka pozemky, mohol by tu vyrásť nový štadión |url=https://sportnet.sme.sk/spravy/futbal-fc-petrzalka-nove-pozemky-stadion-monacobet-liga-2025-2026/ |access-date=2025-10-09 |website=sportnet.sme.sk |language=sk}}"}}
